A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DyPE work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original FLUX and FiTv2 experiments, a 50-rater human study, scheduler ablations, resolution scaling and panoramic generation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds broader baseline comparisons, Qwen-Image experiments, video generation, image editing and attention-entropy measurements.

M1.justification: The core DyPE scheduler and dynamic positional-scaling rules remain unchanged in Eqs. 13–17. v2 additionally evaluates a DY-YaRN+HiFlow inference variant incorporating progressive refinement (Table 3 and Figure 14), a limited procedural extension whose integration details are not supplied.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds video generation evaluated with VBench and multi-reference image editing through multi-concept composition. These substantially extend the previous image-generation tasks. DrawBench, Aesthetic-4K, ImageNet and panoramic generation remain; testing Qwen-Image on Aesthetic-4K does not itself add dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with DemoFusion, FreCaS, DiffuseHigh, I-Max, FLUX+BSRGAN, UltraPixel, Diffusion-4K and HiFlow, retaining FreeScale. TASR already appeared in v1 Appendix B, but v2 extends its participation to DrawBench, additional resolutions, the human study and FiTv2 comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include global and patch FID/IS comparisons at 2048 and 4096 square resolutions, 33-frame Wan2.1 video generation at 1280×720, and editing at 2656×2656. The human study expands from two to three comparison pairs per prompt while retaining 20 prompts and 50 raters. Appendix F introduces a native-resolution attention reference. Existing experiment settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix F adds a focused diagnostic using 20 prompts to test whether high-resolution generation preserves native-resolution attention entropy, reporting timestep curves and mean absolute deviations. The existing scheduler ablations and resolution-limit analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, generation seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new entropy averages and mean absolute errors are diagnostic measurements, not added uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial baseline, Qwen-Image, video, editing and entropy results. Its new TASR human comparison reports DyPE preferences of 70.5%, 80.6% and 94.2%. Shared FLUX, FiTv2, ablation and panorama scores remain unchanged. FreeScale's earlier CLIP, ImageReward and aesthetics scores disappear, while its 4096-resolution FID of 259.24 is retained in the expanded comparison.

T1.justification: The Fourier-mixture formulation, PSD derivation, progression map, assumptions and scaling equations are retained, including the appendix formulas. The new entropy analysis supplies empirical measurements rather than a new mathematical derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and principal conclusion retain the same contribution: training-free dynamic positional extrapolation without additional sampling overhead, with stronger benefits at higher resolutions. The added experiments broaden support without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that DyPE mitigates attention-entropy shift and preserves native-resolution attention behavior. It also identifies GPU memory as limiting video evaluation to 33 frames. The core spectral explanation remains unchanged, while v1's explicit qualification that FreeScale uses an older SDXL backbone is dropped.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly states that code will be released upon acceptance; this is a future commitment, not evidence of released code. The project link, L40S hardware, 28 sampling steps and existing hyperparameters remain. Added experiments identify specific models, including Wan2.1 1.3B and Qwen-Image-Edit-2509.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds discussion of FreeU and FAM-Diffusion and distinguishes RIFLEx's temporal extrapolation from spatial resolution scaling. Additional references accompany the new baselines, models and benchmark; the Frequency-aware Diffusion Models and Improving Image Generation with Better Captions references are removed. The central positioning against static RoPE methods and Lumina-Next remains.

P1.justification: Most foundational exposition is retained. v2 splits Section 4.1 into positional-extrapolation and general-baseline comparisons, adds an Impact Statement and Appendix F, makes local language and reference corrections, and removes video generation from the conclusion's future-work discussion.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Tables gain comparator rows and new experimental panels; new figures cover Qwen-Image, video, editing, general baselines and entropy. Several formerly separate appendix figures are compressed together onto the final page.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons materially address v1's limited evidence against non-positional-extrapolation approaches. Cross-model evaluations and the attention diagnostic further strengthen support for generality and the proposed mechanism. These gains outweigh remaining sparse patch-evaluation and HiFlow integration details and a new reporting inconsistency: the Impact Statement denies human-subject involvement despite the retained 50-rater study.
